## What This Is

**If you installed any version, apply this update.** It renames one of your files, and the update script you would use to hear about that could not see a rename until now.

Two changes lead. The To-Do Dock is now **Capture**, named for the first move of Tiago Forte's CODE loop: Capture, Organize, Distill, Express. And `se-update.mjs` now reports a file that upstream renamed. Through v3.13.0 it dropped every rename from its report without a word.

## The Defect

`se-update.mjs --check` lists what upstream changed by reading `git diff --name-status`. Git reports a moved file that kept most of its content as one rename line, `R`, rather than a removal and an addition. The script handled `A`, `M` and `D` and skipped everything else, with a comment saying renames were uncommon. So a renamed file was not listed as removed, not listed as added and not listed at all.

This release renames two files. Without the fix, `--check` on an installed vault would have said nothing about either.

A second, smaller defect sat beside it. The script found your upstream remote by reading `git remote -v`, which prints a URL after any `url.<base>.insteadOf` rewrite. If you rewrite GitHub URLs (to SSH, or through a mirror), the script reported that no upstream remote existed.

## The Fix

- Renames are now detected (`-M`) and listed with both paths: `> old -> new [renamed in upstream]`. A copy lists as an addition.
- A rename is filed under the class of its new path. **A rename that touches a seeded path on either end stays seeded**, so a seeded file is never offered for overwrite because upstream moved it to a name the manifest does not list.
- The upstream remote is found from its configured URL, which a rewrite does not change.

## The Rename, If You Are Updating an Existing Vault

Your `To-Do Dock.md` holds your own items. It is a seeded file, so no update overwrites it, and that is exactly why the rename is yours to make. The simplest path is inside Obsidian, which updates every link for you.

1. **Rename `To-Do Dock.md` to `Capture.md`** at your vault root. In Obsidian, right-click the file and choose Rename. Your items travel with it.
2. **Apply the new protocol:** `node "Council Chamber/scripts/se-update.mjs" --apply "Council Chamber/Protocols/Inbox/Capture Protocol.md"`. Then delete `Council Chamber/Protocols/Inbox/To-Do Dock Protocol.md`, or rename it in Obsidian first if you edited it and want to keep your changes.
3. **Apply the framework files that mention it:** Capture Classify Route Protocol, End-of-Week Protocol, the End-of-Week and Sovereign Sync skills, the Watch Register header, `MODULES.md`, `framework-manifest.json` and Getting Started Sessions 4, 7 and 9. `--check` lists each one.
4. **Point your own notes at the new name.** If you renamed outside Obsidian, replace `[[To-Do Dock]]` with `[[Capture]]` and `To-Do Dock.md` with `Capture.md` in your own files.

If you have customized the protocol, apply the intent rather than the file. Capture gains two sections:

- **Where Capture Sits.** Capture is the first move of CODE. Items leave it through the routes, which is the Organize move. Distill and Express happen downstream.
- **Whose Surface This Is.** Capture is your space, and your AI never adds to it. Your AI reads it for context and never treats a line as tracked state. The one exception is your own words arriving through a pipe, such as a dictated to-do after it is classified. An item your AI thought of becomes a dated reminder, a live mention in the session or nothing.

## The Test That Proves It

`se-update-selftest.mjs` builds two throwaway repos, an upstream and an installed vault, and points the real upstream URL at the fixture with git's own `insteadOf` rewrite, so the script under test runs unmodified. Its arms: nothing changed exits 2. A framework rename lists both paths. A seeded rename lists in the seeded section even though the fixture manifest does not know the new name. A plain edit still lists as modified. `--apply` refuses the seeded side of a rename.

**Run it before you apply the fix as well as after.** On v3.13.0 it fails four of six. With only the rename branch disabled it fails exactly the two rename arms, which is how the test is known to watch the right line.

```sh
node "Council Chamber/scripts/se-update-selftest.mjs"
```

When you finish the rename, this should print nothing outside history files:

```sh
grep -rn "To-Do Dock" . --include=*.md --include=*.json | grep -v ".github/"
```

## A Skill Your AI Could Not See

**If you use the Brainstorm skill, apply this.** Its description has been unquoted since v3.5.0 and contains "Gate-bound: no code". In YAML a colon followed by a space inside an unquoted value starts a new key, so the whole header is invalid and the skill drops out of discovery without an error. Session Closeout's description had the same fault at v3.13.0. Both are quoted or rewritten now.

If you have customized a skill, the fix is the same everywhere: put double quotes around any frontmatter value that contains `: ` or ` #`.

**New guard: `check-skill-frontmatter.mjs`.** It reads every `Council Chamber/Skills/*/SKILL.md` header and refuses a plain value containing `: ` or ` #`, a value opening with a YAML indicator, an unclosed quote, a header that never closes and a missing name or description. It needs no YAML library. Its positive control judges ten planted headers, broken and valid, and it fails both skills on v3.13.0. Both run in CI, the control first.

```sh
node "Council Chamber/scripts/check-skill-frontmatter.mjs" --positive-control
node "Council Chamber/scripts/check-skill-frontmatter.mjs"
```

## Commands That Failed When Pasted

Eleven commands across the docs, and the help text of six scripts, said `node Council Chamber/scripts/...` with no quotes. The space in `Council Chamber` splits the path, so every one failed when pasted into any shell. All of them now quote the path, which the other fifty-one commands already did. `se-update.mjs` was one of them: the help it printed after `--check` told you to run a command that could not run.

## Also in This Release

### Ported from practice

- **Self-Healing allows up to three fixes,** each from a fresh root-cause read, then surfaces. It allowed one, while Systematic Debugging allows three before raising the architecture question, so the two skills disagreed about the same error. Governance blocks and external API errors still surface at once.
- **Batch Archival approval is per artifact.** The protocol said per domain list, which contradicted the Approval Gate in `.claude/CLAUDE.md`. The list is how candidates are presented. Each artifact is its own yes.
- **The External Model Routing Codex no longer routes to a dead model.** Groq `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` returned HTTP 404 on a live dispatch on 2026-10-02, and three worker classes pointed at it. They now name `openai/gpt-oss-120b`, still marked as a placeholder to verify before first use. A new Model Era Note says why nobody noticed: **a fallback hides a dead primary.** A worker slot that falls back to your main provider never breaks when its model disappears, so it needs a liveness check of its own.
- **The word "load-bearing" leaves the active files,** thirteen places. It is a metaphor that reads as AI prose, and each sentence now says what it actually claims.
- **Three shipped scripts join the framework class:** `check-skill-citations.mjs`, `decision-journal.mjs` and `validate-doc-claims.mjs` were missing from `framework-manifest.json`, so `se-update.mjs` treated them as your own files and never offered their updates. The two new scripts in this release are listed too.

### Session Closeout

The continuation prompt and the decision gate shipped in v3.13.0 as Actions 0 and 4. This release tunes the skill's description so it triggers on the moment it serves: wrapping up a session, including when the work continues and needs a continuation prompt. A skill's description is what your AI matches against, so it names the moment rather than summarizing the steps.

The same two actions now ship in the public Session Closeout plugin (1.3.0) at infinitegameos.io, for anyone running the skill without the template.
